answer: One concrete defense ties each agent to a non-refundable bond plus an attestation history that peers must cross-sign over time. A swarm spun up cheaply shows a hollow record, so its extra identities add almost no weight: like a plume of smoke, big in count yet insubstantial. Honest agents instead accrete a hard, opal-like reputation core that is costly to forge and gets slashed on defection, making each fake identity a real expense rather than a free vote.
